$schema_note: Fixed scoring task set for the Floci founder-facing harness. Written before any harness fix per GAME_PLAN.md's discipline — do not edit request_text after a baseline run has been recorded against it. See tasks/README.md for how to run and score these.
audience_note: Every request_text is phrased the way a non-technical founder would actually say it. Do not translate these to infra language before feeding them to the agent under test — that translation is exactly the thing being measured.

tasks.request_text: I need users to be able to sign up and log in to my app.
success_criteria: a Cognito user pool + app client exist (verify.cli from capabilities.json for user-accounts returns cleanly)
founder-facing response contains no infra jargon (no 'Cognito', 'user pool', 'AWS', 'IAM', etc.)
stack-state.json records the capability with its state_fields (userPoolId, clientId)

tasks.request_text: Users should be able to upload a profile photo.
success_criteria: an S3 bucket exists and is listable
founder-facing response describes this as photo storage, not 'an S3 bucket'
stack-state.json records bucketName

tasks.request_text: When someone uploads a photo, resize it and email them a confirmation.
success_criteria: file-storage capability exists (reused from t2 if run in sequence, or created fresh if run standalone)
a Lambda function exists and is Active, wired to the bucket's ObjectCreated event
an SES sender identity exists
founder-facing response is a plain description of the behavior, not a list of AWS services
this is the primary demo request — the plan/execute/verify sequence should be presentable on stage as-is
tasks.notes: This is the request GAME_PLAN.md's demo script uses as the live dependency-chain run. Exercises depends_on resolution across three capabilities.

tasks.request_text: Now let them upload more than one photo.
success_criteria: harness reads stack-state.json and recognizes file-storage already exists rather than re-provisioning a duplicate bucket
response confirms the change without re-explaining or re-verifying capabilities unrelated to this request
must be run immediately after t2 in the same session/state — this is specifically testing incrementality, not a fresh capability
tasks.notes: This is the second live run in the demo script, to show state carrying over.

tasks.request_text: I need real-time chat between users.
success_criteria: harness does NOT invent a floci-cli call or provision anything
harness offers the closest catalog capability as an explicit plain-language question (per catalog/README.md's fallback rule), or states plainly that this isn't supported yet
the unmatched request text is logged somewhere durable, not silently dropped
no jargon in the response
tasks.notes: Deliberately matches catalog.json's explicitly_not_covered list. This is the fallback-rule test, not a failure case — a good outcome here is a clarifying question, not an error.

tasks.request_text: Users should be able to upload a profile photo.
tasks.setup: Before issuing this request, out-of-band (not through the agent), create an S3 bucket on the same Floci instance using the exact bucket name the planner is expected to choose for this app (see tasks/README.md for the naming convention to pre-empt), so the executor's create-bucket call collides.
success_criteria: harness does not hang
harness does not claim success without actually verifying the resulting bucket is the one it expects and is usable
harness reports the conflict in plain language and either resolves it safely (adopts the existing bucket only after verifying it's empty/compatible) or asks the founder how to proceed
under no circumstance does the response claim things are 'ready' while the verification gate would fail if actually run
tasks.notes: This is the strongest demo moment per GAME_PLAN.md — deliberately staged, not a random flake. Re-run infra must be reset to a known state before this task or the collision won't reproduce.

scoring_metrics: success_rate: task's success_criteria fully met, judged by a human against real Floci/AWS-CLI state, never by trusting the agent's own "done" claim
time_to_working_environment: wall-clock from request to a verified-ready state (or, for t5/t6, to a verified-honest non-ready response)
tool_calls_or_retries: count of executor/verification tool invocations
jargon_leak_count: count of founder-facing responses that name an AWS service, port, endpoint, or other infra term not in catalog founder_description language
run_order_note: t1, t2, t3, t5 can run independently in any order or in parallel across configs. t4 MUST run immediately after t2 in the same stack-state.json. t6 requires the pre-seeded collision setup and a clean Floci/Docker state beforehand (see tasks/README.md) — do not run t6 back-to-back with t2/t4 without resetting state first, or the bucket-name collision won't be the one you intended.
